records.title: S*: Test Time Scaling for Code Generation
records.read_scope: Publisher metadata/abstract and arXiv v1 method3.1/Algorithm1; not full-paper review
records.relevance: Parallel candidates, public-test-driven repair with early stopping, and execution-grounded pairwise input synthesis already exist. Strong later comparator; current BOK3/REPAIR3 are simpler screening controls, not an S* reproduction.

records.title: Adaptive Test-Time Compute Allocation with Evolving In-Context Demonstrations
records.read_scope: Publisher metadata/abstract; arXiv v1 sections4.2 and5.3; not full-paper review
records.relevance: Adaptive allocation and evolving demonstration reuse are established. Main coverage experiments use an oracle correctness reward; selected ablations use other feedback. Preserve information parity: do not import final hidden correctness into online allocation.

records.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
records.venue: arXiv preprint; peer-reviewed venue not verified
records.relevance: Predictive action selection, predictor reliability checks and feedback adaptation already have close precedent. Coding experiments keep the coder fixed and rank four repairs before execution. Matched test usage alone does not establish matched total generation/training cost. Graph-conditional edge maintenance still requires separate evidence and attribution.

records.title: FTDI: A budget-aware self-healing framework for LLM multi-agent code generation
records.read_scope: Crossref identity, publisher-indexed abstract/introduction, author README. Publisher full-text open returned403. Code implementation not yet audited.
records.relevance: Budget gating, static failure diagnosis, tiered repair and historical typed repair priors already address multi-agent coding recovery under injected faults. Generic diagnostic feedback plus budget control is not new. Synthetic fault injection differs from graph-edit-induced credit invalidation; that distinction needs empirical evidence.
